subject: The bellows and its reed block cut open and plotted on a scope graticule, the pleats a triangle trace that closes as pressure rises and the reed tongue a bright stroke lifted over its slot.
controls: press: the moving board slides left and the pleats close up, the bellows shortening from 250 to 140 px; position of the board, shape of the pleat traces.
reed: the bright tongue over plate a swings open from 6 to 32 px at its tip; rotation about its rivet.
leak: a dotted breath trace streams out between the lower pleats, 0 to about 16 dots and longer as it rises; count.
choir: the second tongue on plate b lifts out of unison and its rivet slides along the plate, 0 to 30 px; position, with a ghost beat-trace across ch2 while playing.
reference: library/theseus-tower (line drawing of a known object, one part moves)
risks: Two languages pulling: a section drawing wants solid cut faces and hatching, a scope wants one phosphor line on a graticule. The graticule is 11 x 5 hairlines across the body and could read as a dashboard grid behind the drawing; it may need to drop to corner ticks. The pleats are the brightest thing, not the reed that sings; at 1:1 the tongue is a 2 px stroke 90 px long, which is right but small. Press both moves a board and reshapes two traces, so its key changes on every press turn (two paths re-keyed).
